label: first copied output after <DEL> in length-3 sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost entirely at step t=4 of L=3 sequences, i.e. the step right after <DEL> where the input is the first copied token orig(0) and the output is orig(1). 99% of the mass is at recall_idx 1, and 92% is in L=3 sequences, where about 94% of these steps fire. Weak tail: low-magnitude firing at recall_idx 1 in L=4 sequences (about 7% of the mass, around 0.05-0.2 of max) and at the final step of L=3 sequences (recall_idx 2, about 1% of the mass). Never fires during the original phase, on the delimiter, or at L>=5. Token identity only weakly modulates it (higher rates when the output is o/f/j/z, and rarer when the token is repeated or digits are common); it is not token-selective.

issues: Wrong data store: you asked to run the baseline on features/copy_transcoder_v2_1of5 (the 1/5 subsample). This whole analysis, including my check, used features/copy_gru_v1_neuron_baseline_store, which came from the computed task. Nobody confirmed that this store is your subsampled data, so the result may not apply to the run you asked for.

On that store the core claim holds. Test scores reproduce exactly: precision 0.946, recall 0.736, F1 0.828, mass recall 0.917. The unit fires only in the copy phase, never in the original phase, on <DEL>, or for L>=5. 98.9% of activation mass is at recall_idx 1 and 92.7% is at L=3.

The tail's size is understated. The explanation says the L=4 recall_idx-1 tail fires at 0.05 to 0.2 of max. On test, missed L=4 activations reach about 0.35 of max (e.g. 'x o z c' at 0.35, 'q o o 3' at 0.33). Its share of mass (about 7%) is correct.
The L=4 tail has no clean subclass I could find. Predicates on 'o' tokens gave precision 0.17 to 0.28. (recall_idx==1)&(L<=4) gives precision 0.19 and F1 0.31, so leaving L=4 out is the right call.

One factual claim is wrong: firing is not rarer for digit-heavy sequences. With n_digits>=2 at L=3 and recall_idx 1, precision is 1.0 against 0.946 overall. Repeated output tokens do fire a bit less (0.885). This is minor.
